title: Identifiers, Naming and Scope Basics
learningObjectives: Explain the central rules behind identifiers, naming and scope basics in C.
Identify the relevant types, declarations, operators or library facilities.
Trace a worked example and explain its result.
Recognize common mistakes, portability concerns and unsafe assumptions.
Apply the concept in a small program and test normal and boundary cases.

understand.concept: An identifier is a name used for a program entity such as an object, function, structure tag or typedef name. C identifiers are case-sensitive and must follow lexical rules. Scope determines where a name can be used; linkage determines whether declarations in different scopes or translation units refer to the same entity.
understand.whyItMatters: Good names make code easier to review, while correct scope prevents accidental access and name collisions. Understanding scope is also essential when a program grows into multiple source files.
understand.analogy: Think of a type as a contract that describes what kind of value an object can hold and which operations make sense for it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only an introduction; C types also determine representation, conversions, alignment and constraints.

explain.narrative:
An identifier is a name used for a program entity such as an object, function, structure tag or typedef name. C identifiers are case-sensitive and must follow lexical rules. Scope determines where a name can be used; linkage determines whether declarations in different scopes or translation units refer to the same entity.

Good names make code easier to review, while correct scope prevents accidental access and name collisions. Understanding scope is also essential when a program grows into multiple source files.

When reviewing code, identify the declared types first, then trace conversions and the exact expression being evaluated. Compile with warnings enabled and test boundary values. Do not rely on assumptions about another compiler or machine.

examples.title: Core example
examples.code: int item_count = 3;\nint Item_count = 5;\n/* These are different identifiers. */
examples.explanation: C treats uppercase and lowercase letters as distinct, so the two identifiers name separate objects.

practise.guidedTask: Write a function with a parameter, a local variable and an inner block variable. Mark the scope of each identifier and compile after moving one use outside its scope.
practise.independentTask: Refactor a program with unclear one-letter names into meaningful identifiers. Introduce a deliberate shadowing example and explain why it can make code harder to read.
hints: A block can introduce a nested scope.
Scope and object lifetime are related but not identical concepts.
Use consistent snake_case names for ordinary C objects and functions.
